description: Golden fixture for the scorecard parity section (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3301, slice S12). rows.jsonl is every parity record one real validate run produced, wrapped as parity-ledger/v1 rows exactly as test-harness parity export plus the dev-hermit writer would publish them. committed-cells.json is the parity selection of the run's own Hermit commit. expected-parity.json is scorecard.rs's summary of those rows (the bytes it would write to scorecard/parity.json); the parity_summary_tests fixture test compares the two and names a temporary file holding the actual summary when they differ.
source_root: dev-hermit ignored/validate/artifacts/<run_id>/ on the host named for this fixture in docs/TESTING_ENVIRONMENTS.md under "Named measurement hosts" (retained validate artifacts; not published)
wrapping: Each exported source row became one line: compact JSON of schema "parity-ledger/v1", event_type "parity.record", event_id = sha256("validate\0<run_id>\0<cell>\0<lane>\0<node>"), team, host, emitted_at, producer "validate", run_id, hermit_sha, source_tree_dirty false, then the source row's cell, test_id, backend, verdict, reason and source, then ,"record": followed by the post-pass record text spliced byte-for-byte from parity.jsonl. All 192 records were checked to be byte-identical to a line of the two sources.

fixture_values.note: This run was never published to the ledger, so team, host and emitted_at are fixture values, not a publication record. Every other field is the run's own. host is fixture-host-b, the host directory of the shard the fixture test reads the rows from (parity/hermit/fixture-host-b/2026-09.jsonl); it was the measuring machine's name until scripts/check-portable-paths.sh refused a literal host name in a tracked ci/ file. event_id does not cover host, so no event id changed. The machine is recorded in docs/TESTING_ENVIRONMENTS.md under "Named measurement hosts".

committed_cells.source: ci/compat-envelope/parity-cells.json at d3a0a4ae3d168565595ae4157b25ab8efbb1861a (git blob 18aea875460ed11e173bd48deecde8906599dd95): 1444 cells, 192 of them selected
committed_cells.projection: The selected cells only, each reduced to the three fields the summary reads, in the source's order: git show 18aea875460ed11e173bd48deecde8906599dd95 | python3 -c 'import json,sys; src=json.load(sys.stdin); print(json.dumps({"cells": [{"test_id": c["test_id"], "backend": c["backend"], "selected": c["selected"]} for c in src["cells"] if c["selected"]]}, indent=2))'. The reader tolerates the other fields, so the reduction changes no selected cell; it keeps the fixture small.
committed_cells.note: Every selected id is a retired backend-parity-c id; the summary joins each to its c-programs successor exactly as it joins the rows, so the run reported all 192 cells its commit selects.

expected_summary: parity: 0/192 matched; selected 192 of 192 committed; measured 175; unavailable 17; record-missing 0; mean credit (measured) 0.052; floor credit (selected) 0.047 [inputs not equalized]
expected_summary_check: The totals and every per-backend line were computed independently in Python from rows.jsonl before expected-parity.json was accepted.
expected_parity_origin: expected-parity.json is produced by the code under test and then reviewed; it is never edited by hand. To regenerate it, run the fixture test (rust-script --test ci/compat-envelope/scorecard.rs the_real_run_1953_rows_summarize_to_the_checked_in_expectation); on a difference it writes the actual summary to $TMPDIR/expected-parity-<pid>.json. Review that file's diff against the checked-in one, explain every changed number here, and only then copy it over.
expected_parity_history: Adding the committed selection (S12 review findings E2/E3) and the clean/unequalized credit split (S8) only added fields: conflicting_hermit_shas, committed_unknown, committed_cells_without_row and cells_outside_committed per run; clean_credit_sum, unequalized_credit_sum, clean_mean_credit, unequalized_mean_credit, committed, committed_selected and outside_committed per tally; legacy_dropped_cells at the top level; and "selected 192 of 192 committed; " in each run line. No existing number changed: every credit is unequalized, so unequalized_credit_sum equals credit_sum (kvm 7.678, liteinst 1.375, sabre 0.020, total 9.073 over 175 measured cells = 0.052), and the clean sums are 0.

Replacing the fixture host name (every row's host, and the shard path the fixture test reads them from) with fixture-host-b changed only generated_from.store_sha256, from d2750e52eb70b0bf984f3b4798f05aa32e413261bf3a127f90f8f4de46cbc9b3 to 0520e2ded9f9a86935622f8be288f2387287aad415ad443524d93d6acf9abf93: the store digest covers each shard's path and bytes. The new value was computed independently in Python as sha256(path, NUL, u64 little-endian length, bytes) before the test's output was accepted. No count or credit changed.
